title: IPL cricketer Abishek Porel arrested on rape charge; woman alleges promise of marriage
content: Bengal Police arrested cricketer Abishek Porel on Tuesday in connection with a rape case.  The arrest followed a directive from the Calcutta High Court regarding the complaint.  A medical student alleged a physical relationship on the promise of marriage.  The complaint also includes charges of criminal intimidation and recording intimate moments.  Porel's career is now overshadowed by these ongoing legal proceedings.

title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes an 'August request' to employees
content: Accenture has implemented a new policy allowing employees to carry over their unused vacation days, aiming to bolster business performance as the fiscal year winds down. CEO Julie Sweet has urged employees to maximize their efforts in these critical weeks. However, this adjustment may inadvertently dissuade workers from taking necessary breaks, raising concerns among investors following a decline in new bookings.

title: Mark Zuckerberg's $300M yacht booed over rescue call; clarification issued
content: Mark Zuckerberg's superyacht Launchpad faced criticism after a stranded boat incident. The vessel's crew was reportedly on a different radio channel during the emergency. Help was already en route when the yacht's crew reviewed the assistance request. The yacht, valued at $390 million, was closer to the distressed skiff. Passengers on a nearby cruise ship booed the yacht's perceived inaction.

title: New Haven landfill becomes solar farm powering 200 homes
content: New Haven is transforming a decommissioned landfill into a major solar energy project, installation of 1,920 solar panels that will produce a significant amount of clean energy every year. With anticipated revenue exceeding $1.4 million over two decades, this venture supports New Haven's dedication to enhancing its renewable energy initiatives, ultimately benefitting both the environment and the local economy.

title: Yonkers uncovers buried river, creating 14,000 sq ft of aquatic habitat
content: In 2012, Yonkers, New York, completed a project to uncover a section of the Saw Mill River that had been buried beneath a downtown parking lot since the 1920s. The former Larkin Plaza was turned into a three-acre public park. Within six months, the restored river supported 14,000 square feet of new aquatic habitat and several species.

title: Anthropic researcher thanks Claude for solving 87-year-old Math conjecture
content: An Anthropic researcher used the AI model Claude Fable 5 to find a counterexample. This discovery challenges the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture in mathematics. The AI-assisted finding reportedly offers a simple counterexample for verification. The conjecture, proposed in two dimensions, was extended to all dimensions later. This AI breakthrough highlights its growing role in mathematical discovery.

title: Kitchen confidential: Rot, raids and reality checks from Mumbai and Bengaluru
content: Recent inspections revealed expired food and poor hygiene in Bengaluru kitchens. Mumbai also saw increased enforcement targeting food outlets and warehouses. These violations highlight systemic issues throughout the food supply chain. Luxury hotels are not exempt from these critical food safety concerns. Effective monitoring and follow-up are essential for ensuring consumer safety.

title: Overtake, chase, hockey sticks, baseball bats: Mumbai man attacked in road rage
content: A fitness trainer and his wife were traumatized by a road-rage incident in Bandra. Five men in an SUV allegedly assaulted the trainer and damaged his car. The incident began when the accused vehicle obstructed the trainer's path. Police detained three individuals and registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation into the matter is currently underway.

title: Kangana slams Naseeruddin: 'Hai iss desh ke, ladte hai padosi desh ke liye'
content: A heated exchange has ignited between Naseeruddin Shah and Piyush Mishra, drawing Kangana Ranaut into the fray as she backs Mishra. This controversy escalated after Shah previously admonished Bollywood for its silence on student protests. In response, Mishra challenged Shah's own record on similar issues, leading Ranaut to launch a fierce critique, branding Shah a fox.

title: ‘You guys cheat’: Pathan reveals Sangakkara clash that turned ‘personal’
content: Irfan Pathan reminisced about a heated exchange with Kumar Sangakkara during a 2005 Test match over a changed cricket ball. What started as personal sledging led to Pathan responding fiercely while scoring 93 runs. Although the tension could have soured their relationship, a later encounter in the IPL with Kings XI Punjab allowed Pathan to extend an apology, paving the way for their newfound friendship.

title: Jana Nayagan box office day 20: Vijay’s film nears Rs194 crore in India
content: Thalapathy Vijay's final film 'Jana Nayagan' continues its theatrical run.  The movie has achieved a significant India net collection of Rs 193.18 crore.  Its worldwide gross collection has now reached Rs 318.09 crore.  Overseas markets have contributed Rs 93.20 crore to the film's total.  The political action drama stars Pooja Hegde and Bobby Deol.

title: ‘Preparation’: Sooryavanshi sweats it out in nets ahead of Duleep Trophy | Watch
content: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is gearing up for the Duleep Trophy following a standout performance in Zimbabwe, where he emerged as India's top run-scorer. Appointed as the vice-captain for the East Zone team, this role not only acknowledges his talent but is designed to prepare him for future leadership. The Duleep Trophy will be an important opportunity for Sooryavanshi to hone his skills in longer format cricket.

title: Ex-India batter questions Sarfaraz’s exile, backs him over Jurel for SL Tests
content: Mohammad Kaif stands firmly in support of Sarfaraz Khan being chosen for India's Test team, emphasising his skill in playing spin bowling. He proposes that Sarfaraz should ideally bat in the five or six position, especially considering Jurel's variable form lately. With the first Test approaching, the selection conundrum is a pivotal discussion in the cricket community.

title: Rio turns discarded salon hair into barriers that protect mangroves from oil
content: Discarded human hair is now preventing oil pollution in Rio de Janeiro's Guanabara Bay.  Each gram of hair absorbs approximately five grams of oil, repelling water effectively.  These hair barriers, made from salon waste, can remain in the water for four months.  The initiative protects vulnerable mangrove ecosystems from chronic and everyday oil leaks.  This innovative project aims to aid the recovery of the bay's marine life.

title: Op Safed Sagar: How IAF took the fight to Pakistan at 18,000 feet in Kargil
content: The Indian Air Force launched Operation Safed Sagar against Pakistani intruders.  Pilots faced unprecedented challenges fighting at extreme altitudes.  Early setbacks led to tactical reassessments and technological adaptations.  Mirage-2000 aircraft with laser-guided bombs proved highly effective.  These air attacks significantly aided ground troops in recapturing key peaks.

title: Faulty Ola scooter, no proper service: Consumer panel orders Rs 1.04 lakh refund
content: A Kerala consumer commission found Ola Electric guilty of service deficiency and unfair trade practices.  The commission ordered Ola Electric to refund the scooter's full purchase price.  This decision followed repeated scooter defects and a lack of proper after-sales support.  The customer experienced significant financial loss and mental stress due to these issues.  Ola Electric must now pay compensation and complaint costs within thirty days.

title: ‘The ideal move’: Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo joins Liverpool on loan
content: Ronald Araujo, the captain of Barcelona, has officially joined Liverpool on a season-long loan, labeling the transition as an ideal choice for his professional journey right now. He agreed to a pay reduction to make the transfer to Anfield possible. Liverpool have confirmed the arrangement, which includes a future option for a permanent deal, adding much-needed depth and experience to their defense.

title: 'Nai naveli dulhan ho': Faculty remark sparks scrutiny after junior doctor’s death
content: Four faculty members at Surat Government Medical College received show-cause notices. An inquiry followed the suicide of postgraduate student Dr Harsh Pandya. Students reported harassment by senior residents to faculty members. The committee found faculty failed to resolve tensions and create harmony. The college council approved the report for submission to the state government.

title: In 1868, an eclipse in India revealed an element found on Earth 27 years later
content: During the solar eclipse of 1868 in India, astronomers stumbled upon an enigmatic yellow spectral line, initially observed by Pierre Jules Janssen. Although its significance was not immediately recognized, Norman Lockyer soon named the unidentified element helium upon further analysis. Eventually, William Ramsay verified helium's presence on Earth in 1895 by extracting it from a mineral, solidifying Janssen's pioneering approach to studying solar prominences.

title: League points will stick around: Why opening games are crucial at Hockey World Cup
content: The upcoming FIH Men’s and Women’s World Cups in Belgium and the Netherlands will be played under a new three-stage format, making the league phase even more crucial as points earned in the opening round will be carried forward to the next stage. That is, the result achieved against a team played in the league counts for the final ranking in the new pool in the next phase.

title: ‘The biggest peak of my sporting life’: Bindra reflects on historic Olympic gold
content: Indian shooting icon Abhinav Bindra commemorated the 18th anniversary of his remarkable gold medal victory at the Beijing Olympics. He reflected on this individual medal as the pinnacle of his athletic journey. Bindra’s victory not only brought glory to him but also ended a lengthy pursuit for India’s individual Olympic gold. Post-retirement, he actively promotes sports in India through his foundation.

title: A note, 5-star hotel, an affair: What led Bengaluru man to kill his 2 daughters
content: A father allegedly killed his two minor daughters in a Bengaluru hotel room. He then attempted suicide, leaving a note citing marital dispute and infidelity. Hotel staff discovered the deceased children and the injured father after no response. The father, identified as S G Imran, is currently receiving medical treatment. Police are investigating the tragic incident and examining evidence from the hotel.

title: Honey Singh calls Badshah 'meri nalayak aulaad' after old clip resurfaces

title: Rain lashes parts of Delhi-NCR; IMD issues yellow alert

Temperatures remained slightly below normal and close to the seasonal average. The maximum temperature is forecast to stay around 33 degrees Celsius. Further showers are likely in several areas of Delhi-NCR.

title: CWG medals, state silence? How actively are states promoting sports and athletes

This investigation tracks the social-media activity of state sports bodies, revealing glaring gaps, from Rajasthan’s last Facebook post in 2012 and Manipur’s silence to Haryana’s limited outreach. In contrast, states like Tamil Nadu show how one can promote grassroots athletes consistently on social media.

title: Watch: Drop Shot Ep. 4 | Jana Nayagan Fever, The Keeper of the Wells & Gaurav Gupta’s Light Song
content:
In this episode, we capture the excitement surrounding Vijay’s Jana Nayagan as fans celebrate what could be the actor’s final film and director H. Vinoth shares insights into the much-awaited release. 
We then explore The Keeper of the Wells, as Chennai-based author Zhayynn James discusses his debut novel inspired by the historic Seven Wells neighbourhood of North Chennai.
